verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's proxy documents logging request input, output, and exceptions to many destinations (Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, S3, DataDog and others), and it tracks per-request metadata such as spend alongside those logs. Inspecting the logs relies on those downstream tools, and latency and token counts are never shown attached to logged requests. missing for 10: evidence that latency and token counts are recorded per logged request, a first-party view in the admin UI for inspecting logged requests and responses, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can inspect logged requests and responses with latency, token counts, and cost attached

citations.quote: Log Proxy input, output, and exceptions using: Langfuse OpenTelemetry GCS, s3, Azure (Blob) Buckets
